data.title: Canaan Inc. Earnings Call Highlights Liquidity Amid Pressure
data.description:
Canaan Inc. ((CAN)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Canaan Inc.’s latest earnings call painted a mixed picture for investors. Management emphasized stronger liquidity, disciplined cost control and positive cash generation from mining projects. Yet these positives were overshadowed by a harsh Bitcoin mining backdrop, revenue below guidance, a steep cut to third-quarter expectations and ongoing pressure on equipment demand and pricing.

Mining Operations Became the Primary Revenue Contributor

Mining has clearly become the core of Canaan’s business model. Second-quarter mining revenue reached about USD 18 million, roughly 55% of total revenue, as the company mined 243 Bitcoins. Importantly, mining income continued to cover direct power and hosting costs, and excluding depreciation, mining gross margin stood at a modest but positive 20%.

Improved Cash Position and Liquidity Management

Despite weaker top-line results, Canaan strengthened its balance sheet. Cash rose to USD 66 million at the end of Q2, up from USD 43 million in Q1, a gain of about USD 23 million. The company collected USD 54 million from product sales and secured an additional USD 15 million from tax refunds, equity distributions and Bitcoin-backed financing, underscoring careful liquidity management.

Operating Expense Reduction

Management continued to tighten the cost base in response to industry headwinds. Excluding sizeable impairment and credit loss charges, operating expenses fell to USD 28.2 million, down 9% sequentially and 14% year over year. Executives stressed ongoing discipline in expense and inventory management, with a renewed focus on preserving cash flow amid volatile Bitcoin economics.

Record Digital Asset Treasury at Quarter End

Canaan further built its digital asset war chest during the period. By the end of June, the company held 1,915 Bitcoins and 3,952 ETH in its treasury, marking another record level of crypto holdings. Based on carrying values, this portfolio was worth about USD 112 million, giving the company a meaningful asset base that can be monetized when needed.

Share Repurchase Program Progress

The company continued to return capital to shareholders despite market turbulence. Year to date, Canaan repurchased around 16.4 million ADSs for USD 7.4 million, including 2.8 million ADSs in the first half and 13.6 million ADSs in late August. The buybacks, funded partly by selling digital assets under a USD 30 million authorization, signal management’s confidence in long-term value.

Project ABC Expansion and Positive Cash Flow

Project ABC again proved to be a bright spot for Canaan’s operations. The joint initiative generated positive cash flow while the partners upgraded the mining fleet, with installed hash rate reaching 4.85 exahash per second at July’s end, up 10% from March. The company received USD 5.2 million in cash from the project in Q2, lifting cumulative cash inflows to USD 8.4 million by late August.

Competitive Mining Power Costs and Fleet Upgrade Plans

Canaan highlighted competitive power economics as a key advantage in a low-margin mining environment. Non-joint-venture hash rate stood at about 10.05 exahash per second at the end of June, while average all-in power costs remained low at roughly USD 0.043 per kilowatt hour. Management plans to deploy at least part of its newer A16 machines next year, which are more energy efficient than the current A15 fleet.

Continued Product and Technology Development

Beyond mining, the company is still investing in hardware innovation. Canaan advanced its A16 series during the quarter, focusing on air-cooled models that can be deployed cheaply and hydro-cooled machines that can run at higher temperatures. Management said it is evaluating full life-cycle economics, including power usage, reliability and maintenance, to sharpen product competitiveness.

Compute-to-Heat Applications Expanded

Canaan’s compute-to-heat strategy gained traction in the Nordic region. The company reported 2 megawatts of equipment already in operation for heating projects, with customers ordering another 6 megawatts in March 2026. Management said the early Nordic deployment validated the use of hydro-cooled mining hardware to supply district heating, hinting at new business models beyond pure mining.

Avalon Home Product Launch Preparation

The Avalon Home line remained small but strategically important as a consumer-facing offering. It generated around USD 1 million of revenue in Q2, reflecting its early stage and strong seasonality. Canaan continued research and development and prepared for mass production of updated home heating products in Q3, aiming to time new launches for the Christmas shopping season.

Gigawatt-Scale Power Resource Objective Maintained

Even as current markets remain tough, Canaan is positioning for scale. Management reiterated confidence in securing gigawatt-scale power resources by the end of 2026, focusing on multiple projects in North America. The company is evaluating acquisition, joint venture and joint development structures, prioritizing low long-term power costs, grid access and stable local policy environments.

Capital Discipline in Future Infrastructure Development

Executives underscored a cautious approach to capital-intensive infrastructure. Canaan said it will avoid pursuing full end-to-end AI or high-performance computing data centers that exceed its capabilities or funding capacity. Instead, it aims to work with partners where it can add value and may contribute existing mining machines as capital to projects, progressing step by step.

Revenue Missed Prior Guidance

Second-quarter results underperformed management’s own expectations. Total revenue came in at about USD 32 million, below the earlier guidance range of USD 35 million to USD 45 million. Management blamed the miss on a sharp Bitcoin price drop late in the quarter, cautious miner equipment purchases, elevated industry inventories and intensifying price competition.

Weak Bitcoin Mining Market Conditions

The call underscored how volatile crypto markets are weighing on fundamentals. Bitcoin climbed from around USD 62,000 to USD 82,000 early in the quarter before falling to roughly USD 58,000 by quarter end. Hash price swung between USD 0.028 and USD 0.039 per terahash per second per day and stayed at low levels, limiting profitability for miners and their suppliers.

Mining Machine Demand and Pricing Remained Under Pressure

Demand for Canaan’s mining equipment slowed sharply, hurting product revenue. In the quarter, the company sold 2.5 exahash per second of computing power at an average price of USD 5.5 per terahash per second, generating about USD 14 million. Elevated industry inventory kept pricing under pressure, pushing down both volumes and average selling prices.

Cautious Third-Quarter Revenue Outlook

Looking ahead, management warned that near-term conditions will stay difficult. Canaan expects Q3 2026 revenue to fall to between USD 11 million and USD 15 million, a sharp drop from Q2 levels. The guidance reflects continued cautious miner procurement, excess inventory that still needs to clear and mining machine prices that remain under pressure across the industry.

Adjusted EBITDA Loss and Significant Accounting Charges

Profitability remained deeply negative despite operational progress. Adjusted EBITDA showed a loss of USD 74.9 million in Q2, roughly unchanged from the prior quarter. Results were weighed down by large non-cash items, including inventory write-downs, property impairment and fair value losses on digital assets, alongside USD 9.2 million in impairment charges and USD 2.7 million in credit losses.

Project ABC Equity Investment Loss

Project ABC delivered cash but also produced accounting headwinds. The retirement of older mining machines and related accounting treatment resulted in roughly USD 4 million of equity investment losses for the project in Q2. Management framed these charges as part of upgrading the fleet for better long-term efficiency, though they still weighed on reported earnings.

Broader Global Demand Has Not Recovered

Canaan’s sales challenges extend well beyond its domestic market. Management reported that mining rig demand outside the U.S. remained very weak, with no meaningful improvement despite Bitcoin’s recent price gains. Weaker mining economics, regulatory developments and geopolitical uncertainty are all curbing customers’ ability and willingness to invest in new hardware.

Avalon Home Sales Showed Seasonality

The Avalon Home business is subject to sharp seasonal swings. After the winter heating season ended, sales of these home heating products dropped noticeably, and management stressed that the segment is still small relative to the total company. Its future revenue share will largely depend on heating cycles and the performance of Canaan’s other lines of business.

Nasdaq Minimum Bid Price Compliance Risk

Listing status emerged as a notable concern for equity holders. Canaan transferred to the Nasdaq Capital Market and secured an additional grace period to regain compliance with the exchange’s minimum bid price rules, pushing the deadline into early 2027. Management pledged to monitor the ADS trading price closely and take steps to maintain its Nasdaq listing.

Power and HPC Projects Remain at an Early and Uncertain Stage

The company’s ambitions in power and high-performance computing are still in their infancy. Management said securing large-scale power resources has become more complex and competitive, with key issues unresolved even for the most advanced projects. Canaan has yet to close another deal comparable to Project ABC or finalize specific partnership models such as co-location or GPU cloud rental.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Priorities

Management’s outlook combines cautious near-term expectations with longer-term ambition. Canaan guided Q3 2026 revenue to USD 11 million to USD 15 million amid continued pricing pressure on miners and softer demand, while planning mass production of new Avalon Home products and future deployment of A16 machines to its mining fleet. The company reiterated confidence in securing gigawatt-scale power load by 2026, even as it refrained from committing to a specific future revenue mix.

Canaan’s earnings call will likely leave investors with a conflicted view. Liquidity, mining operations and strategic projects such as compute-to-heat and Project ABC are moving in the right direction, and management is exercising clear capital discipline. Yet persistent losses, a weak equipment cycle, cautious guidance and Nasdaq compliance risk underline the challenges facing the stock in the current Bitcoin mining downturn.

data.title: G-III Apparel Earnings Call Highlights Brand-Led Transition
data.description:
G-Iii Apparel ((GIII)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

G-III Apparel’s latest earnings call struck a cautiously optimistic tone. Management highlighted a solid earnings beat, sharp margin expansion and a fortified balance sheet, even as reported sales declined and legacy Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger revenue continued to roll off. Investors heard confidence in the go-forward brand portfolio and in the Marc Jacobs deal, despite near-term dilution and European weakness.

Second-Quarter Earnings Beat Guidance

Non-GAAP earnings per diluted share came in at $0.26, topping guidance of $0.15 to $0.25 and signaling stronger profitability than expected. Executives credited disciplined execution, tighter expense control and favorable mix as key factors, underscoring the company’s ability to deliver earnings growth even in a challenging demand backdrop.

Gross Margin Expanded Sharply

Gross margin jumped to 45.2% from 40.8% a year ago, a roughly 440 basis-point improvement that investors will view as a major highlight. The gains came from targeted price increases, healthier full-price selling and a deliberate push toward higher-margin owned brands, supported by ongoing cost-savings initiatives across sourcing and operations.

Go-Forward Portfolio Shows Resilience

Excluding Tommy Hilfiger and Calvin Klein, the go-forward brand portfolio posted high single-digit growth in the quarter. Wholesale sales in full-price channels for these brands climbed more than 20%, suggesting that the company’s future-facing platform is gaining traction even as legacy licensed revenue fades.

Marc Jacobs Acquisition Marks Strategic Pivot

Management framed the Marc Jacobs acquisition as transformational, positioning G-III as a brand-led global apparel powerhouse. The company now owns 100% of the Marc Jacobs operating business and holds a 50% earnings stake in the brand’s licensing via a joint venture with WHP Global, deepening its exposure to premium fashion.

Marc Jacobs Growth Avenues

Marc Jacobs currently derives roughly 90% of sales from handbags, small leather goods and accessories, leaving ample room to expand into new categories. G-III plans to grow ready-to-wear, fragrance, beauty, eyewear, children’s apparel, licensing and international wholesale, leveraging a network of more than 100 owned stores and strong direct-to-consumer economics.

Long-Term Marc Jacobs Revenue Potential

The Marc Jacobs operating business is expected to deliver about $360 million in global sales this year, excluding licensing income. Over the long term, management believes Marc Jacobs can scale to $1 billion in annual revenue for G-III, making it a central pillar of the company’s brand portfolio strategy.

Balance Sheet Strength and Liquidity

G-III ended the quarter with roughly $529 million in cash, up sharply from $302 million last year, and about $1 billion in available liquidity. Cash was boosted by around $134 million in tariff refunds including interest, and management emphasized that the balance sheet remains healthy even after the Marc Jacobs purchase, giving room to invest in growth.

Inventory Discipline and Capital Returns

Inventory fell about 13% versus a year ago, reflecting tighter inventory management and reduced risk of markdowns. The company also returned more than $12 million to shareholders through buybacks and dividends in the quarter, signaling confidence in its financial position while maintaining flexibility for strategic spending.

Donna Karan Performance Stands Out

Donna Karan delivered more than 45% sales growth in the quarter, fueled by strong consumer demand and aspirational positioning at full price. Digital traffic, conversion and average unit retail all improved, handbags posted double-digit gains and the dress business emerged as a key driver within the brand.

DKNY Maintains Solid Momentum

DKNY.com revenue rose in the mid-20% range year over year, supported by higher conversion and healthy average unit retail growth. Brick-and-mortar DKNY stores saw mid-single-digit comparable sales gains, while retail partners increased space allocations for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027, signaling confidence in the brand’s trajectory.

Karl Lagerfeld Extends Lifestyle Reach

Karl Lagerfeld posted strong growth in North America led by wholesale, and margins improved in Europe thanks to pricing and channel mix. The Karl Lagerfeld Jeans line continued to outperform internationally, while the brand pushed deeper into lifestyle with the first Karl Lagerfeld Café in Amsterdam and new residences and hotel projects.

Vilebrequin Delivers High Margins

Vilebrequin recorded positive growth across Europe, the Caribbean and Asia, with brand margins exceeding internal targets. Higher average unit retails and solid demand underpinned performance, complemented by a second limited-edition Fiat Topolino collaboration and the opening of the Vilebrequin La Plage Miami beach club.

Licensed Sports and Contemporary Brands Gain

The sports and lifestyle platform delivered healthy growth, helped by Starter’s limited-edition Pokémon jacket at Target and expanding Converse distribution. Levi’s was singled out as a quarterly highlight, while the contemporary portfolio, including French Connection and BCBG, continued to build momentum.

Strategic Investments and Cost Efficiencies

Management is investing in people, technology, marketing, Marc Jacobs product development, digital capabilities and retail experience to fuel future growth. At the same time, G-III plans to pursue previously announced cost-saving initiatives and identify new efficiencies, aiming to balance investment spending with margin preservation.

Sales Declines and PVH License Impact

Quarterly net sales fell about 10% to roughly $554 million and came in slightly below plan, largely due to planned reductions in Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger revenue. Since PVH announced it would reclaim those licenses, G-III expects to have lost nearly $1.2 billion in revenue by year-end, with guidance embedding substantial ongoing declines.

European Market Challenges

Management described Europe as a difficult environment, citing macro softness, sharply lower traffic and heightened promotional activity. Struggling department stores in England, weaker travel from the Middle East and unusually warm weather weighed on sales, adding regional pressure on top of the PVH license wind-down.

Third-Quarter Headwinds and Earnings Decline

For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, G-III expects net sales of about $870 million versus $989 million a year ago, reflecting the biggest year-over-year reduction in PVH-related revenue. Non-GAAP net income is forecast at $59 million to $64 million, or $1.35 to $1.45 per share, down from $1.90 per share last year as the transition away from PVH weighs on earnings.

Initial Dilution from Marc Jacobs

Management acknowledged that Marc Jacobs will be dilutive for the first 12 months and slightly dilutive for the rest of fiscal 2027. However, the deal is expected to turn accretive thereafter, and leadership positioned the near-term drag as an acceptable cost to secure a high-potential, brand-centric growth engine.

Retail Margin and SG&A Pressure

Retail gross margin slipped to 50.6% from 52.4% last year, hurt by higher promotional activity during the quarter. SG&A expenses rose to $231 million from $227 million, excluding acquisition costs, as the company continued investing in talent, technology and marketing, causing some expense deleverage despite warehouse efficiency gains.

Tariffs and Delivery Timing Issues

Management flagged that tariffs impacted the business in a significant way last year and remain a headwind, with guidance assuming current rates persist. Weather-related delivery delays and missed containers also affected the timing of second-quarter sales, though the company expects most of that business to shift into subsequent periods.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Outlook

G-III reiterated fiscal 2027 net sales guidance of about $2.71 billion, down roughly 8% year over year, while raising non-GAAP EPS to $2.20 to $2.30 and adjusted EBITDA to $174 million to $178 million. The company anticipates close to 400 basis points of full-year gross margin improvement, net interest income of about $5 million, capex near $40 million and no further share repurchases, as Marc Jacobs scales toward a long-term $1 billion opportunity.

G-III’s earnings call painted a picture of a company in transition, trading near-term revenue and margin noise for a stronger brand-led future. With Donna Karan, DKNY, Karl Lagerfeld and Vilebrequin gaining traction, and Marc Jacobs positioned as a potential $1 billion-plus anchor, investors will be watching execution closely as PVH license losses roll off and margin gains become the key driver of shareholder value.
